title: Test the Pyramid with Real Data

scenes.tts: The first film followed energy through the Bay. Do real measurements shrink in the same neat pattern? Test the model with one measured ecosystem.
scenes.visual: Reuse the first film's moving Bay and organism colours. In this film the bars are coloured by feeding level: energy and sunlight GOLD; producers GREEN; first-order consumers BLUE; second-order consumers ORANGE; third-order consumers PURPLE; decomposers GREY; heat RED. A tidy four-bar pyramid rises over the water, each bar exactly one tenth of the bar below. Stamp it 'classroom model'. Then make the bars wobble into question-mark outlines. Show 'Do real steps match?'
scenes.narration: The first film followed energy through the Bay. Do real measurements shrink in the same neat pattern? Test the model with one measured ecosystem.

scenes.visual: Keep water, plankton, and sunlight moving behind a dark band. Show only 'Test the Pyramid with Real Data', then transform the Bay into a clear spring.

scenes.tts: The measurements come from Silver Springs, Florida. Researchers estimated yearly energy entering each feeding level. The values were rough, but they let us test the pyramid's shape. Each value combines many lives across a shared area.
scenes.visual: Transform the Bay into a clear spring cross-section while preserving object positions and colours. Show plants and algae in GREEN along the bottom, small plant eaters in BLUE, larger consumers in ORANGE, and top consumers in PURPLE. A calendar page cycles through seasons without spoken numbers. Label the whole picture 'rough yearly estimates'.
scenes.narration: The measurements come from Silver Springs, Florida. Researchers estimated yearly energy entering each feeding level. The values were rough, but they let us test the pyramid's shape. Each value combines many lives across a shared area.

scenes.tts: Start with energy captured by plants and algae. Their green bar fills most of the frame. This is the producer level and the base for the consumer paths. Everything above depends on this incoming supply.
scenes.visual: Pull GOLD sunlight into the GREEN producers. Transform that glow into a wide GREEN horizontal bar. Compute its width from the table value shown only on screen: 'Producers 20,810'. Add 'kilocalories per square meter per year' beneath the axis. Mark the diagram 'computed from lesson table'.
scenes.narration: Start with energy captured by plants and algae. Their green bar fills most of the frame. This is the producer level and the base for the consumer paths. Everything above depends on this incoming supply.

scenes.tts: Now add the consumers in order. Each measured bar is narrower than the one below. A narrower bar means less energy entered that level. Yet the bars do not shrink by one identical fraction.
scenes.visual: Grow the BLUE, ORANGE, and PURPLE bars above the producer bar, with widths computed from the displayed values. Give every bar a minimum visible width and show the small note 'thin bars enlarged to be visible'. Show only on screen: 'First-order 3,368', 'Second-order 383', and 'Third-order 21'. Keep a thin ruler line moving across their ends to make the unequal ratios visible.
scenes.narration: Now add the consumers in order. Each measured bar is narrower than the one below. A narrower bar means less energy entered that level. Yet the bars do not shrink by one identical fraction.

scenes.tts: Calculate each transfer by dividing a level by the one below it. Each result describes only one jump between neighboring levels. A fixed law would make every result match. The uneven bars already hint otherwise.
scenes.visual: Beside each gap, animate a division card using the table values, but leave each result covered by a neutral question panel. Use the same GOLD highlight for every division arrow. Add a thin dashed marker labelled '10% classroom model'.
scenes.narration: Calculate each transfer by dividing a level by the one below it. Each result describes only one jump between neighboring levels. A fixed law would make every result match. The uneven bars already hint otherwise.

scenes.tts: Will the three calculated percentages match exactly, or will they differ? Choose before the results appear. Use each neighboring pair in the stack.
scenes.visual: Keep the three covered result panels beside their divisions. Put two large neutral choices above them: 'match exactly' and 'differ'. Show the question 'Same fraction every time?' Keep water shimmer and a slowly moving ruler, but reveal no answer.
scenes.narration: Will the three calculated percentages match exactly, or will they differ? Choose before the results appear. Use each neighboring pair in the stack.

scenes.visual: Thinking pause. Hold both choices neutral and keep every result covered. The dashed model marker glows softly while the spring water and organisms continue slow movement.

scenes.tts: They differ. The three measured steps land in different places around the model marker. Real transfer varies even within one ecosystem. No single measured step defines the whole web.
scenes.visual: Brighten 'differ' and uncover the computed results only on screen: '16.2%', '11.4%', and '5.5%'. Under the 16.2% card add a small footnote: 'of all energy captured (see producer row)'. Place them beside the dashed model marker without highlighting a closest result. Then return all three to the energy bars, leaving their unequal gaps visible.
scenes.narration: They differ. The three measured steps land in different places around the model marker. Real transfer varies even within one ecosystem. No single measured step defines the whole web.

scenes.tts: The missing energy did not vanish. Organisms released much as heat during life processes. Uneaten material and wastes carried stored energy into a decomposer side branch. Decomposers receive material from the whole web, so they sit beside the stack.
scenes.visual: From every coloured bar, peel broad RED waves outward and send GREY dashed material routes downward. Build a separate GREY decomposer bar beside the pyramid, not above it. Show its lesson value only on screen: 'Decomposers 5,060'. Label it 'side branch from all levels'.
scenes.narration: The missing energy did not vanish. Organisms released much as heat during life processes. Uneaten material and wastes carried stored energy into a decomposer side branch. Decomposers receive material from the whole web, so they sit beside the stack.

scenes.tts: The producer row needs special care. It counts all captured energy. Plants used much themselves, so only part became new plant material that consumers could eat. That smaller block is the producer material available for growth and feeding.
scenes.visual: Split the GREEN producer bar into a broad RED respiration stream and a smaller GREEN block. Show only on screen: 'captured 20,810', 'respiration 11,977', and 'new plant material 8,833'. Keep the consumer bars connected to the new-material block. Mark the split 'energy accounting'.
scenes.narration: The producer row needs special care. It counts all captured energy. Plants used much themselves, so only part became new plant material that consumers could eat. That smaller block is the producer material available for growth and feeding.

scenes.tts: These bars measure energy flow, not animal counts. One large organism and many small ones can use similar totals. They came from one spring and rough estimates. The pattern can guide a claim without predicting an exact population.
scenes.visual: Place a large crossed-out label 'head count' beside the energy axis. Frame the spring with 'one place' and the table with 'rough estimates'. Transform several small consumer cartoons into one larger cartoon while keeping their shared energy bar unchanged. Mark the example 'schematic'.
scenes.narration: These bars measure energy flow, not animal counts. One large organism and many small ones can use similar totals. They came from one spring and rough estimates. The pattern can guide a claim without predicting an exact population.

scenes.tts: Return to the Bay. Different feeding steps can pass different fractions. The exact width may change, but the upward supply narrows. Repeating those losses still leaves far less energy near an osprey than near the producers.
scenes.visual: Transform the spring back into the first film's Bay. Overlay three unequal shrinking steps on GOLD packets moving from GREEN to BLUE, ORANGE, and PURPLE. A large ORANGE school crosses the centre while one PURPLE osprey circles above.
scenes.narration: Return to the Bay. Different feeding steps can pass different fractions. The exact width may change, but the upward supply narrows. Repeating those losses still leaves far less energy near an osprey than near the producers.

scenes.tts: The measurements refine the classroom model without changing its main pattern. At each feeding step, less energy is available to the next level. Use the rule for direction, then use data for size. Every step passes on less energy, but how much less varies.
scenes.visual: Place the measured spring bars beside the Bay web, both filling the frame. Run one last GOLD pulse upward through each. On the guiding rule, align the narrowing steps and remove every other label.
scenes.narration: The measurements refine the classroom model without changing its main pattern. At each feeding step, less energy is available to the next level. Use the rule for direction, then use data for size. Every step passes on less energy, but how much less varies.

scenes.visual: Dim both worlds and show one line only: 'Every step passes on less energy, but how much less varies.'
